text.p: Italian bond futures closed firmer but off session highs in a quiet, cautious market stuck in a narrow range awaiting domestic economic and political developments, traders said.

"There was renewed buying of Btp futures when the Italian market came back in today after seeing heavy selling on LIFFE on Monday. But the cash market lagged behind lacking ideas," one London based trader said. "Sentiment is not as positive as at the end of the year," he added noting the market was still expecting a Bank of Italy discount rate cut but there was uncertainty about current metalworkers' wage talks.

Trades unions and employers in the engineering and metalworking sector were holding separate meetings on Tuesday over their long-running pay dispute. Formal talks with the government were due to resume on Wednesday.

National statistics body Istat is due to issue official CPI data for December on Wednesday with forecasts based on preliminary data indicating a year-on-year rate of 2.5/2.6 percent against November's 2.6 percent.

Traders noted Prime Minister Romano Prodi today warned that inflation data for January will not be good because of statistical reasons but the figures would improve in February. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
